title: Cryptography

objectives.text: Choose between symmetric encryption, asymmetric encryption, hashing, MACs and digital signatures for a given security goal
State block size, key sizes and current status of DES, 3DES, AES, Blowfish, Twofish, RC4 and ChaCha20, and the weakness of ECB
Compare RSA, Diffie-Hellman and ECC, match key sizes to security strength, and name the NIST post-quantum standards
Explain PKI components, X.509 fields, chain of trust and revocation (CRL, OCSP), and create a self-signed certificate
Describe what TLS 1.3 removed and added, and contrast S/MIME with PGP and the main disk encryption tools
Classify a cryptanalysis scenario by attack model and name the attack (birthday, meet-in-the-middle, rainbow table, side channel, padding oracle, downgrade)
Recognize blockchain and quantum computing attacks and the tools used for cryptanalysis and TLS auditing
Recommend fixes for weak algorithms, key handling, password storage and TLS configuration, and outline a post-quantum migration

readingMap.why: Algorithm, key size and hash facts are asked directly; learn the tables and the symmetric vs asymmetric rules.
PKI, certificates, TLS, S/MIME vs PGP and disk encryption tools come up in many scenario questions.
Attack models and named attacks are easy points once you can tell them apart; skim the tool screenshots.
Mostly the reverse of the attacks section; focus on password storage, key management and TLS settings.

labs.name: Encrypt, hash and sign files with OpenSSL and GnuPG
labs.skill: Symmetric file encryption with a password-derived key, hashing, and GPG key pairs, encryption and signatures on your own machine

labs.name: Create a self-signed certificate and inspect a real certificate chain
labs.skill: openssl req -x509, openssl x509 -text and openssl s_client to read issuer, subject, SAN and validity

labs.name: Audit the TLS configuration of your own test server
labs.skill: Listing protocol versions, cipher suites and known TLS weaknesses with testssl.sh and Nmap ssl-enum-ciphers

labs.name: Explore classical and modern ciphers in CrypTool Online
labs.skill: Frequency analysis on a substitution cipher and seeing why ECB leaks patterns

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a friend how HTTPS lets two strangers agree on a secret key over the internet, and what the certificate adds that Diffie-Hellman alone cannot.
Explain why passwords are stored with a salted, slow hash instead of being encrypted, and how a salt defeats rainbow tables.
Explain why a large quantum computer threatens RSA and ECC far more than AES, and what 'harvest now, decrypt later' means for data you encrypt today.
